title: Safe embedded run to a stopped configuration
statement: Let $k$ be a natural number, let $S$ and $H$ be state sets, let $w$ be a Boolean input word, and let $tm$ and $host$ be machines with $k$ work tapes over the Boolean alphabet. Suppose $emb:S\to H$ and $anchor\in H$ satisfy $emb(q)\ne anchor$ for every $q\in S$; suppose also that every configuration of $tm$ whose state is a stopped state is fixed by one step, and that for each non-stopped state $q$, the transition of $host$ at $emb(q)$ is the state-renaming of the transition of $tm$ at $q$, for every input symbol and tuple of work-tape symbols. If a configuration $d$ has a stopped state and is reached from a configuration $c$ of $tm$ after $T$ steps, then there is some $t\le T$ such that running $host$ from the state-renaming of $c$ for $t$ steps gives the state-renaming of $d$, and at every time $j\le t$ the state of that host computation is different from $anchor$.
hypotheses_covered: Natural number $k$, state sets $S,H$, and Boolean input word $w$.
Machines $tm$ and $host$ with $k$ work tapes over Booleans.
State map $emb:S\to H$ and anchor state $anchor\in H$.
Every configuration of $tm$ in a stopped state is fixed by one step.
For every non-stopped $q$ and all input and work symbols, the host transition at $emb(q)$ equals the state-renamed transition of $tm$ at $q$.
The state of $d$ is a stopped state.
